answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks through enclave attestation, requiring nodes to run within certified secure hardware. Attackers incur the scarce cost of buying physical silicon dies per identity rather than spawning a plume of virtual clones. Auditors check these signatures across a defensive ridge, layering proofs like a pearl around each agent's binary. However, this relies on centralized chipmakers and remains vulnerable to side-channel key theft.
